questions.q: Which feature marks every insertion and deletion made by co-authors?
questions.solution: **Track Changes** (Review tab, Ctrl+Shift+E) records each edit so reviewers can accept or reject it later.

questions.q:
Consider the statements:
1. POST runs before the boot loader.
2. Warm booting restarts the machine without switching off the power.
3. The BIOS loads the operating system directly into the Recycle Bin.
Which are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are the standard booting facts. Statement 3 is nonsense — the boot loader loads the **kernel into RAM**; the Recycle Bin is a desktop folder for deleted files.
questions.shortcut: One absurd statement marks the wrong set.

questions.q: EPROM differs from PROM because it can be erased by:
questions.solution: EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM) is erased by exposing the quartz window to ultraviolet light. PROM cannot be erased once programmed; EEPROM is the electrically erasable version.
questions.shortcut: One E = light (EPROM, UV); two E's = electricity (EEPROM).

questions.q: The typical default address typed to open a home router's settings page is —
questions.solution: Home routers commonly sit at **192.168.1.1** — a private Class C address.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  ENERVATE
questions.solution: **Enervate** = to drain of strength = weaken. It looks like 'energy' but points the other way; 'energise' is the planted trap.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: After the helper **did**, the base form is required: part 2 must be **end** ('did the lecture end'). The no-sooner…than frame in parts 3 and 4 is correctly built.
questions.shortcut: did + base verb; than pairs with no sooner.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The list of candidates ___ been published.
questions.solution: The head noun is **list** (singular); the of-phrase does not change it → has been published.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Achievement** = achieve + ment. The pair makes an 'ee' sound after h (not c), so it is **ie**, and the e of achieve stays before the consonant suffix -ment.
questions.shortcut: No c before the 'ee' pair -> ie; achieve keeps its e.

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification of living organisms was proposed by:
questions.solution: **R.H. Whittaker** proposed the five kingdoms — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — in **1969**. Linnaeus gave binomial nomenclature and the two-kingdom system.
questions.shortcut: My Pet Fish Plays Alone — Whittaker.

questions.q: A nutcracker is an example of which class of lever?
questions.solution: In a nutcracker the **load (nut) lies between** the hinge (fulcrum) and the hands (effort), making it a **class 2** lever, like a wheelbarrow and a bottle opener.

questions.q: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the seven SI base units?
questions.solution: The base units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela. The **newton** is derived: 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².
questions.shortcut: Named after a person but not in the 7-list = derived (only kelvin and ampere are both).

questions.q: The **First Five Year Plan** (1951-56) was based on the —
questions.solution: The 1st plan used the **Harrod-Domar** growth model and gave top priority to agriculture and irrigation — a success thanks to good monsoons.

questions.q: A wooden cube of side $4$ cm is cut into unit cubes (edge $1$ cm). How many small cubes are formed?
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{4}{1}\right)^3 = 64$ unit cubes.
questions.shortcut: $4^3 = 64$. Trap: $16$ — that is one FACE of small cubes ($4^2$).

questions.q: A can complete a job in 3 days and B in 6 days. They work on alternate days, A starting on day 1. The job is finished in:
questions.solution: Per 2-day cycle: $\frac13 + \frac16 = \frac12$. Two cycles = 4 days complete the job exactly.

questions.q: A is 3 times as efficient as B, and together they finish a work in 12 days. A alone will finish it in:
The value of $\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$ is:
questions.solution: $\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta=1$, so the expression $=1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta$.

questions.q: **P walks 6 km East and then 8 km South. Q walks 6 km West and then 8 km North from the same starting point. In which direction is Q from P?**
questions.solution: P = (6 E, 8 S); Q = (6 W, 8 N). From P to Q: ΔE = −12 (West), ΔN = +16 (North) → **North-West**.
questions.shortcut: 'Q from P' = stand at P; the arrow to Q has both components — combine the words.

questions.q: How many letters of the word **BACKGROUND** look exactly the same in a water image (considered one by one)?
questions.solution: Top-bottom symmetric capitals: B C D E H I K O X. Letter by letter in B A C K G R O U N D: B ✓, A ✗, C ✓, K ✓, G ✗, R ✗, O ✓, U ✗, N ✗, D ✓ → **5**.

questions.q: **A man walks 6 km East, then 6 km North, then 12 km South. How far is he from his starting point?**
questions.solution: Net legs: 6 E; North: 6 − 12 = −6 (net 6 South). Distance = $\sqrt{6^2+6^2}$ = **6√2 km**.
questions.shortcut: 6-6 legs at right angles → hypotenuse is leg×√2.
